_comment: WHICH BRANCHES MAY NOT REACH master ON AI JUDGEMENT ALONE.
Written 2026-09-13 after six capability-branch merges landed on master in one session
without Tom's word. His ruling: 'Really you should never merge a major branch to master
without my all-clear on completion.' The harm is not a broken build -- every one of those
merges was green -- it is that GREEN IS NOT DONE. A passing suite says the code works; it
says nothing about whether the FEATURE is finished, and only Tom can answer that.
A branch listed here needs a matching entry in dev/branch-all-clears.json, pinned to the
exact commit cleared, before dev/hooks/pre-merge-commit will let it into master.
A branch NOT listed here is an ordinary track -- a defect fix, a doc change, a tooling
change -- and merges on the existing rules: green check_all on the merge result, and the
pre-push stamp. That distinction is the whole design. Do not list everything; a gate that
stops all work is a gate somebody switches off.
_protected_comment: EVERY FEATURE BRANCH ALIVE TODAY IS LISTED, and until 2026-09-17 only five were.
The six feat/* branches built on 2026-09-16 were held back by a SENTENCE in
dev/session-handoff.md -- 'SIX FEATURE BRANCHES ARE BUILT AND AWAIT HIS BROWSER PASS.
NONE MAY MERGE' -- and by nothing else. That is prose holding a rule, which is the exact
arrangement this file exists because of: on 2026-09-13 six capability merges landed on
master, every one of them green, because a session read its own passing build as the
answer to 'is this done'. A session that skips the handoff -- which has happened, and is
why that file grew a STOP header -- would have found nothing in its way.
SO THE RULE IS NOW: a branch whose purpose is a FEATURE goes in this list when it is
made, not when somebody remembers. A defect, tooling or documentation track does not,
and must not -- a gate that stops all work is a gate somebody switches off, which is
case 8c of branch_policy_selftest.php and the case that matters most.
customer, graph and custom-property were DELETED on Tom's word (2026-09-16) and their
names stay here deliberately: a listed branch that does not exist costs nothing, and a
name that comes back meaning something else must not walk through an open door.

feature_freeze.lifted_by: Tom, 2026-09-17, answering 'Does the feature freeze come off?' with 'Lift it now', and telling the session in his next turn that his answers were done. His recorded choice -- not an inference from silence, and not an AI reading its own green build as permission.
feature_freeze.lifted_note: IT CAME OFF BECAUSE release/ewb NOW EXISTS, which is the reason he was given and accepted: a freeze stops everybody, a release branch stops nobody. LIFTING IT MERGES NOTHING BY ITSELF. Every branch in 'protected' still needs his all-clear in dev/branch-all-clears.json, pinned to the exact commit, and that lock is untouched. The two were never one key, which was his own point on 2026-09-15.
feature_freeze.why: Tom, 2026-09-15: "Remember that we are in a feature freeze. I will test. But even if I were to approve a merge, the scripts must block it until the freeze is removed. Right?" As built the answer was NO -- an all-clear was the only lock, so his approval and the freeze were one key. It is two locks now.
_comment: THE FEATURE FREEZE, AND IT IS NOT THE EMERGENCY 'freeze' BELOW.
This refuses a merge of any branch in 'protected' -- which is to say a FEATURE -- and
refuses it EVEN WHEN Tom's all-clear for that exact commit is on file. His approval says
the feature is finished; this says it is not the week to ship it. The approval keeps
standing and the merge goes through when the freeze lifts, provided the branch has not
moved since he cleared it.
IT LEAVES DEFECT WORK ALONE, and that separation is the entire reason it is a second
flag rather than 'freeze.active'. Setting that one on stops every merge but a 'hotfix:',
which on 2026-09-13 cost a full day of bug fixes he was waiting for: 'what I am hearing
from you blocks bug fixes, and that is unacceptable.' A gate that stops all work is a
gate somebody switches off.
ONLY TOM LIFTS IT, in a turn where he has said so. An AI clearing its own freeze is the
2026-09-13 failure wearing a different hat.
THE FREEZE IS A FEATURE FREEZE. IT HAS NEVER BEEN A MERGE FREEZE, AND READING IT AS ONE
BLOCKS BUG FIXES -- which are the entire content of these days.
Tom's plan, stated 2026-09-10 and repeated 2026-09-14 because this repository kept getting
it wrong: freeze FEATURES on 10 September; fix bugs through 14 September; translate on the
14th; then keep fixing bugs AND DEPLOYING THEM through 16 September.
So a bug fix merges to master on the ordinary rules -- green check_all on the merge result
-- and master must stay PULLABLE, because he is pulling it every day. What may not merge is
a FEATURE, and the 'protected' list above is the whole mechanism for that: a capability
branch needs his all-clear.
'active: true' stops EVERY merge but a 'hotfix:'. That is an emergency instrument and it is
OFF. It was ON from 2026-09-13 to 2026-09-14 on a misreading of 'we can't do that if we are
merging our work to master' -- 'our work' meant the capability branches, not the bug fixes
he was waiting on. Tom, 2026-09-14: 'what I am hearing from you blocks bug fixes, and that
is unacceptable.' Do not set it true again without his word.
